title: February-March warmth gave no clear leaf-to-bloom interval link in four US samples from 1965 to 2008
abstract: We tested whether warmer February-March conditions were linked to a shorter time from first leaf to first bloom. We paired public lilac and honeysuckle records with NOAA gridded temperature. Four separate East/West and early/late models used 14,154 plant-years from 1965 to 2008, with plant and year effects. Interval slopes ranged from -0.192 to +0.461 days per C. All four uncertainty intervals included zero after adjustment for four tests. Both leaf and bloom dates moved earlier in warmer conditions. The eastern gap slopes were positive when year effects were omitted, which limits attribution to local temperature. Taxon coverage, missing visits, selected long records, coarse seasonal temperature, and approximate cluster intervals limit inference. This is a conditional weather test. It does not identify climate-change or pollution effects. The package preserves the selected panel, source hashes, code, all fitted results, a figure, and an independent numerical check.

display.caption: Interval estimates with plant and year effects. Bars are approximate 95% family-wise intervals for four tests. All four include zero.
